This is usually [[ISO 843|transliterated letter-for-letter]] back into the [[Latin alphabet]] as ''Antetokounmpo''. The same applies to his middle name ''Entoumpouisi'', which stems from the Greek transliteration of ''[[Ndubuisi]]''.}} November 20, 1997){{Cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/126901/sid/12474/tid/291/_/2016_FIBA_U20_European_Championship_Division_B/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180326141630/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/126901/sid/12474/tid/291/_/2016_FIBA_U20_European_Championship_Division_B/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 26, 2018|title=Ndubuisi Antetokounmpo profile, FIBA U20 European Championship 2016|website=FIBA.COM|accessdate=March 14, 2023}} is a Nigerian-Greek professional [[basketball]] player for [[Aris B.C.|Aris Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. Antetokounmpo played [[college basketball]] for the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]]. He was drafted 60th overall by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]], and his draft rights were then traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. He won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2020. His brothers [[Giannis Antetokounmpo|Giannis]], [[Thanasis Antetokounmpo|Thanasis]] and [[Alex Antetokounmpo|Alex]] are also professional basketball players. Kostas, along with his brothers, [[Giannis Antetokounmpo|Giannis]], [[Thanasis Antetokounmpo|Thanasis]] and [[Alex Antetokounmpo|Alex]], and hockey player [[Filip Forsberg]], was announced as joining the [[Nashville SC]] ownership group in the [[Major League Soccer|MLS]].{{cite tweet|user=MLS|number=1631295244565204993|title=All joining the @NashvilleSC ownership group. Welcome to MLS!}} ==Early life and family== Antetokounmpo was born in [[Sepolia]] in [[Athens]], Greece. His parents were immigrants from [[Nigeria]]. His late father, Charles, was a former Nigerian [[association football|soccer]] player, while his mother, Veronica, was a [[high jumper]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/2013/09/26/226268651/nbas-g-bo-wants-to-bring-hope-to-greece-and-to-milwaukee|title=NBA Rookie Wants To Bring Hope To Greece, And To Milwaukee|publisher=NPR|access-date=May 31, 2018}} Charles died in September 2017, at age 54.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974785|title=Trail Blazers vs. Bucks – Game Recap – October 21, 2017|publisher=ESPN|access-date=May 31, 2018}} His parents are from different Nigerian ethnic groups; Charles was [[Yoruba people|Yoruba]], and Veronica is [[Igbo people|Igbo]].{{cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/bucks-giannis-antetokounmpo-greek-freak-wants-to-go-back-to-his-nigerian-roots/ |title='The Greek Freak' wants to go back to his Nigerian roots |first=Marc J. |last=Spears |publisher=[[Andscape]] |date=March 5, 2019 |access-date=March 8, 2019}} He has a Nigerian passport, granted to him in June 2013 so that he could gain a [[visa policy of the United States|visa]], and be allowed to legally enter the United States.{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.gr/basketball/article/916698/i-halasmeni-kafetiera|title=Η χαλασμένη καφετιέρα | Blog - Νίκος Παπαδογιάννης | Gazzetta|website=www.gazzetta.gr|accessdate=March 14, 2023}} He officially became a full Greek citizen in 2016.{{Cite web|url=http://www.matrix24.gr/2016/01/vgazi-elliniko-diavatirio-o-kostas-antetokounmpo/|title=Βγάζει ελληνικό διαβατήριο ο Κώστας Αντετοκούνμπο|date=January 25, 2016|website=Matrix24|accessdate=March 14, 2023}} He is the younger brother of basketball players [[Giannis Antetokounmpo|Giannis]] and [[Thanasis Antetokounmpo|Thanasis]] and the older brother of [[Alex Antetokounmpo|Alex]].{{cite web|last1=Archdeacon|first1=Tom|title=Flyers' Kostas Antetokounmpo tries to live up to his name|url=https://www.mydaytondailynews.com/sports/tom-archdeacon-flyers-kostas-antetokounmpo-tries-live-his-name/meHZJCKf9vQXNYVhHne5gL/|website=[[Dayton Daily News]]|access-date=March 22, 2018|date=September 23, 2017|archive-date=June 21, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621043031/https://www.mydaytondailynews.com/sports/tom-archdeacon-flyers-kostas-antetokounmpo-tries-live-his-name/meHZJCKf9vQXNYVhHne5gL/|url-status=dead}} His oldest brother, Francis, is also a professional association football player. He began playing basketball with the junior teams of [[Filathlitikos BC|Filathlitikos]], in Athens.{{cn|date=May 2025}} ==High school career== After his older brother [[Giannis Antetokounmpo|Giannis]] was drafted by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2013 NBA draft]], Antetokounmpo, along with his parents and his younger brother, Alexis, moved to Milwaukee. He attended [[Dominican High School (Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin)|Dominican High School]] in [[Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin]],{{cite web|last1=Stewart|first1=Mark|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo making a name for himself at Dominican|url=http://archive.jsonline.com/sports/preps/kostas-antetokounmpo-making-a-name-for-himself-at-dominican-b99670083z1-368913091.html/|website=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|access-date=March 22, 2018|date=February 15, 2016}} where he played high school basketball during his junior and senior years. As a senior, he led his team to a state championship.{{Cite web|url=http://daytonflyers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4218|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo – 2016–17|access-date=May 31, 2018}} ==College career== After high school, Antetokounmpo moved on to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Dayton]]. In the [[2016–17 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|2016–17 season]], his first with the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Flyers]], he was [[redshirt (college sports)|red-shirted]],{{Cite news|url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2016/10/3/13148932/dayton-flyers-kostas-antetokounmpo-ineligible-redshirt-ncaa|title=Dayton's Kostas Antetokounmpo ruled ineligible for 2016–17|work=Mid-Major Madness|access-date=May 31, 2018}} after being ruled a "partial qualifier",{{Cite news|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2016/10/03/kostas-antetokounmpo-ruled-ineligible-for-dayton/|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo ruled ineligible for Dayton|date=October 3, 2016|work=CollegeBasketballTalk|access-date=May 31, 2018}} due to having spent his first two years of high school in Greece.[https://flyerfaithful.com/kostas-antetokounmpo-may-have-to-sit-the-2016-17-season-out-88140697b419 Kostas Antetokounmpo may have to sit the 2016–17 season out]{{Dead link|date=February 2020 web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kostas-antetokounmpo-1.html|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo College Stats {{!}} College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|access-date=May 31, 2018}} averaging 5.2 points, 2.9 rebounds, 0.4 assists, 0.2 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game, in 15.1 minutes per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4066490/kostas-antetokounmpo|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo|publisher=ESPN|access-date=May 31, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2018–2019)=== On March 22, 2018, Antetokounmpo declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=Givony|first1=Jonathan|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo to test NBA draft waters|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22873095/kostas-antetokounmpo-dayton-flyers-enter-nba-draft-test-waters|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=March 22, 2018|date=March 22, 2018}} On May 4, 2018, Antetokounmpo was one of a record-high 69 players to enter the [[NBA Draft Combine]].{{Cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/complete-2018-nba-draft-combine-list-211843026.html|title=Some of college basketball's biggest names highlight NBA draft combine list|access-date=May 31, 2018}} Antetokounmpo was projected to be a second round selection, similar to his older brother [[Thanasis Antetokounmpo|Thanasis]]. He was the last pick of the [[2018 NBA draft]], selected by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and then immediately traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite news|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-draft-drought-ends-antetokounmpo-chosen-with-last-pick/LWtNcq9ztfmGFeZQZ9tS9L/|title=Dayton draft drought ends as Antetokounmpo chosen with last pick|newspaper=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 22, 2018|first=David|last=Jablonski}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-acquire-draft-rights-to-ray-spalding-and-kostas-antetokounmpo/|title=Mavericks acquire draft rights to Ray Spalding and Kostas Antetokounmpo|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 21, 2018|publisher=mavs.com}} Antetokounmpo signed a [[two-way contract]] on July 13. Throughout the contract, he would split his playing time between the Mavericks and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|title=Mavericks sign Kostas Antetokounmpo to two-way contract; waive Jalen Jones|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-kostas-antetokounmpo-to-two-way-contract-waive-jalen-jones/|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=July 13, 2018}} During his time in the G-League, he averaged 12.3 points and 7 rebounds per game, earning him the nickname “Mr Fantastic” by Legends Radio Announcer Quinn Redmond. He made his NBA debut on March 20, 2019, in a 118–126 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Lillard scores 33 points, Blazers beat Mavericks 126–118|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071746|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 20, 2019|access-date=March 20, 2019}} On July 19, 2019, Antetokounmpo was waived by the Mavericks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mavsmoneyball.com/2019/7/19/20701354/dallas-mavericks-waive-kostas-antetokounmpo=21|title=Mavericks waive Kostas Antetokounmpo|date=July 19, 2019|website=mavsmoneyball.com|access-date=July 19, 2019}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2019–2021)=== Antetokounmpo was claimed off waivers by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on July 22, 2019.{{cite web |title=Report: Lakers claim Kostas Antetokounmpo off free agency waivers |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/07/21/report-lakers-claim-kostas-antetokounmpo-waivers |website=NBA |access-date=22 July 2019}}{{cite web |title=Lakers Awarded Kostas Antetokounmpo on Waiver Claim |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/190722-lakers-awarded-kostas-antetokounmpo-waiver-claim |website=Los Angeles Lakers |access-date=22 July 2019}} He played 5 games throughout the season on a [[two-way contract]] and scored a career high 7 points in the team's 136–122 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]] on August 13, 2020.{{Cite web|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/antetko01.html|access-date=2020-08-15|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}} Antetokounmpo won his first championship after the Lakers defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in six games. He became the first Greek-born player to win an NBA championship, with his brothers Giannis and Thanasis winning their own championships with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] the next season. On November 26, 2020, Antetokounmpo re-signed with the Lakers to a two-way contract.{{Cite web |date=26 November 2020 |title=Lakers Re-sign Kostas Antetokounmpo |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-resign-kostas-antetokounmpo-free-agency2021 |access-date=27 November 2020 |website=Los Angeles Lakers}} ===ASVEL (2021–2022)=== On July 16, 2021, Antetokounmpo signed with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL Villeurbanne]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite news|first=Alessandro|last=Maggi|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo signs with Asvel|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/kostas-antetokounmpo-signs-with-asvel/|newspaper=Sportando|date=July 16, 2021|accessdate=July 16, 2021}} In 26 [[EuroLeague]] games, he averaged 5.8 points, 2.6 rebounds and 0.7 blocks, playing around 13 minutes per contest. ===Chicago Bulls (2022)=== On October 14, 2022, Antetokounmpo signed a two-way contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2022 |title=Bulls Sign Kostas Antetokounmpo to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-kostas-antetokounmpo-to-two-way-contract |access-date=October 15, 2022 |website=NBA}} He was waived by the Bulls on December 16, 2022, without appearing in a game for the team at the NBA level.{{Cite web |date=December 16, 2022 |title=Bulls sign Carlik Jones to a Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-carlik-jones-to-a-two-way-contract |access-date=December 16, 2022 |website=NBA}} ===Fenerbahçe (2022–2023)=== On December 19, 2022, Antetokounmpo signed with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe Beko]] of the [[Basketball Super League|Turkish Basketball Super League]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2022/12/kostas-antetokounmpo-fenerbahce-beko-da|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo Fenerbahçe Beko'da|last=|first=|date=December 19, 2022|website=|publisher=[[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]]|language=tr|access-date=December 19, 2022}} In 14 [[EuroLeague]] games, he averaged 2.7 points and 0.8 rebounds, playing around 7 minutes per contest. On June 20, 2023, he mutually parted ways with the club. ===Panathinaikos (2023–2025)=== On June 22, 2023, Antetokounmpo signed a two-year contract with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]], where his older brother [[Thanasis Antetokounmpo|Thanasis]] had previously played for two seasons.[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1520281/kostas-antetokounmpo-panathinaikos-euroleague/ Kostas Antetokounmpo officially moves to Panathinaikos for two years] On February 5, 2025, coach [[Ergin Ataman]] announced that Antetokounmpo would be parting ways with the defending [[EuroLeague]] champions. On February 11, 2025, he mutually parted ways with the team.{{cite web | last=Stroggylakis | first=Antonis | title=Panathinaikos officially parts ways with Kostas Antetokounmpo | website=Eurohoops | date=2025-02-11 | url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1784654/panathinaikos-officially-parts-ways-with-kostas-antetokounmpo/ | access-date=2025-09-20}} ===UCAM Murcia (2025)=== Antetokounmpo finished out the [[2024–25 ACB season|2024–2025 campaign]] playing for Spanish club [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and [[Basketball Champions League|BCL]], signing in February 2025.{{Cite web|title=Kostas Antetokoumpo nuevo jugador del UCAM Murcia CB |url=https://www.ucamdeportes.com/ucamcb/noticias/kostas-antetokoumpo-nuevo-jugador-del-ucam-murcia-cb|date=February 12, 2025|access-date=January 5, 2025|website=ucamdeportes.com|language=es}} ===Olympiacos (2025–2026)=== On July 10, 2025, Antetokounmpo signed a two-year contract with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]].{{Cite web|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo seals move to Olympiacos|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/kostas-antetokounmpo-seals-move-to-olympiacos/|access-date=July 16, 2025|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|language=en}} ====Loan to Aris (2026)==== On January 4, 2026, it was announced that Antetokounmpo would be loaned out to [[Aris B.C.|Aris]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. The news came as [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] announced the signing of [[Tyrique Jones]].{{Cite web |last=Armakola |first=Konstantina |date=January 5, 2026 |title=Άρης Betsson, μεταγραφές: Ο Κώστας Αντετοκούνμπο μετακομίζει στο Αλεξάνδρειο |url=https://www.sport24.gr/basket/aris-metagrafes-o-kostas-antetokounmpo-metakomizei-sto-alexandreio/ |url-status=live |access-date=January 5, 2026 |website=sport24.gr |language=el}} The move was officially announced by Olympiacos on January 9, 2026.{{cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/kostas-antetokounmpo-moves-from-olympiacos-to-aris/|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo moves from Olympiacos to Aris |publisher=EuroLeague|date=January 9, 2026|accessdate=January 9, 2026}} ===Aris (2026–present)=== On July 5, 2026, Antetokounmpo signed a three–year deal with [[Aris B.C.|Aris Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{cite web|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo at ARIS Betsson until 2029|url=https://arisbasketball.com/en/first-team/kostas-antetokounmpo-at-aris-betsson-until-2029.html|website=arisbasketball.com|date=July 5, 2026|access-date=July 5, 2026}} ==National team career== ===Greek junior national team=== Antetokounmpo played with the junior [[Greece men's national under-20 basketball team|Greek Under-20 national team]]. He played at the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship Division B]], where he won a bronze medal.{{Cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/Ndubuisi%20ADETOKUNBO/pid/126901/_//players.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180326141604/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/Ndubuisi%20ADETOKUNBO/pid/126901/_//players.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 26, 2018|title=archive.fiba.com: Players|website=archive.fiba.com|access-date=May 31, 2018}} During the tournament, he averaged 1.3 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 0.3 assists per game.{{Cite news|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/126901/sid/12474/tid/291/_/2016_FIBA_U20_European_Championship_Division_B/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180326141630/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/126901/sid/12474/tid/291/_/2016_FIBA_U20_European_Championship_Division_B/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 26, 2018|title=Ndubuisi Antetokounmpo profile, FIBA U20 European Championship 2016|work=FIBA.COM|access-date=May 31, 2018}} ===Greek senior national team=== Antetokounmpo played with the senior men's [[Greek men's national basketball team|Greek national team]] at the [[2020 FIBA Men's Olympic Qualifying Tournaments – Victoria|2020 Victoria FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]], and at the [[EuroBasket 2022]]. ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {| class="wikitable" |- | style="background:#AFE6BA;
